title: Classification & Logistic Regression
why: Most business ML problems are classification: fraud, churn, spam, diagnosis. Logistic regression is the baseline you always beat first.
explain: Logistic regression turns a linear score z = w.x + b into a probability with the sigmoid function 1 / (1 + e^-z). You predict class 1 when the probability passes a threshold. The default is 0.5, but the right threshold depends on the costs of each kind of mistake.

Its loss is binary cross-entropy: -[y log p + (1 - y) log(1 - p)]. It punishes confident wrong answers very heavily. The gradient has a neat form, (1/n) X^T (p - y): the same shape as linear regression's gradient, with predicted probabilities in place of raw predictions.

For more than two classes, softmax converts a vector of scores into probabilities that sum to one, and cross-entropy is computed over classes. The decision boundary of logistic regression is linear; to bend it, engineer features or move to nonlinear models.
key_points: Sigmoid for binary problems, softmax for multi-class
Cross-entropy is the negative log-likelihood of the labels
The threshold is a business decision, not a constant
For imbalanced data, reweight classes or resample
pitfalls: Treating predicted probabilities as calibrated without checking

leetcode.why: Binary search over sorted scores is how you find a decision threshold.
Three-way partitioning is the same operation as splitting examples into classes.
The majority-element algorithm is the simplest possible classifier baseline.
Counting and selecting the most frequent class or label is a constant companion in evaluation code.

industry.q: Why use cross-entropy instead of mean squared error for classification?
key_points: MSE with a sigmoid has vanishing gradients when the model is confidently wrong
Cross-entropy is the maximum-likelihood loss for Bernoulli labels and is convex for logistic regression
It gives a stronger, better-behaved gradient signal

industry.q: Your classifier reports 99% accuracy but the positive class is 1% of the data. What do you do?
key_points: Always predicting negative also scores 99%, so accuracy is misleading
Reweight, resample or move the threshold
Tie the choice to the business cost of each error

industry.q: Write predict_proba and the loss for binary logistic regression with NumPy and no Python loops.
key_points: Clip p to [eps, 1 - eps] before the logs
Return shape (n,) and keep y the same shape
